claims.text: Colchicine, an NSAID or an oral corticosteroid are the three first-line flare treatments, strongly recommended
claims.quote: Using colchicine, NSAIDs, or glucocorticoids (oral, intraarticular, or intramuscular) as appropriate first-line therapy for gout flares over IL-1 inhibitors or adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) is strongly recommended

claims.text: Guideline does not rank the three; choice driven by patient factors (other conditions, access, past experience)
claims.quote: the Voting Panel did not further prioritize between the first-line agents, noting that treatment selection should be driven by patient factors (e.g., comorbidity, access, past experience)

claims.text: Lowering urate is a separate job; the guideline cautions against conflating flare management and ULT
claims.quote: the possibility of information over-load for patients, which may lead to conflating flare management and long-term ULT

claims.text: First-line drugs work particularly well when given early after symptom onset
claims.quote: tolerability of these agents in flare management, particularly when administered early after symptom onset

claims.text: FDA-approved colchicine flare dosing (1.2 mg then 0.6 mg an hour later) should be followed
claims.quote: For colchicine specifically, the FDA-approved dosing should be followed (1.2 mg immediately followed by 0.6 mg an hour later, with ongoing antiinflammatory therapy until the flare resolves).

claims.text: Low-dose over high-dose colchicine strongly recommended
claims.quote: Given similar efficacy and a lower risk of adverse effects, low-dose colchicine over high-dose colchicine is strongly recommended when colchicine is the chosen agent.

claims.text: Dose and duration chosen partly by flare severity
claims.quote: Appropriate dosing and duration should be guided by the severity of the flare.

claims.text: Topical ice conditionally recommended as an adjunct to first-line medicine
claims.quote: Using topical ice as an adjuvant treatment over no adjuvant treatment is conditionally recommended for patients experiencing a gout flare.

claims.text: Supporting data for ice are limited
claims.quote: Noting limited supporting data (), the Voting Panel recommended the use of topical ice as an adjuvant therapy for flares.

claims.text: Limiting alcohol conditionally recommended for everyone with gout
claims.quote: Limiting alcohol intake is conditionally recommended for patients with gout, regardless of disease activity.

claims.text: More than 1 to 2 drinks in prior 24 hours linked to 40 percent higher flare risk
claims.quote: consuming >1–2 alcoholic beverage servings in the prior 24 hours was associated with a 40% higher risk of gout flare than periods without alcohol consumption

claims.text: Prophylaxis strongly recommended when starting ULT; options include colchicine, NSAID, prednisone or prednisolone
claims.quote: Administering concomitant antiinflammatory prophylaxis therapy (e.g., colchicine, nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs [NSAIDs], prednisone/prednisolone) over no antiinflammatory prophylaxis therapy is strongly recommended.

claims.text: Prophylaxis for at least 3 to 6 months
claims.quote: When initiating ULT, concomitant antiinflammatory prophylaxis therapy for a duration of at least 3-6 months was strongly recommended.

claims.text: When ULT is indicated, starting it during the flare conditionally recommended over waiting
claims.quote: When the decision is made that ULT is indicated while the patient is experiencing a gout flare, starting ULT during the gout flare over starting ULT after the gout flare has resolved is conditionally recommended.

claims.text: ULT for tophi, radiographic damage, or 2 or more flares a year
claims.quote: Initiating ULT is strongly recommended for gout patients with any of the following: ≥1 subcutaneous tophi; evidence of radiographic damage (any modality) attributable to gout; OR frequent gout flares, with frequent being defined as ≥2 annually.

claims.text: Allopurinol preferred; treat-to-target below 6 mg/dL
claims.quote: a treat-to-target management strategy with ULT dose titration guided by serial serum urate (SU) measurements, with an SU target of <6 mg/dl

claims.text: ULT reduces flare frequency and tophi
claims.quote: there was high certainty of evidence regarding the efficacy of ULT in reducing flare frequency (–), tophi (,), and SU concentrations (–)

claims.text: Weight loss program if overweight conditionally recommended
claims.quote: Using a weight loss program (no specific program endorsed) is conditionally recommended for those patients with gout who are overweight/obese, regardless of disease activity.

claims.text: Limiting high-fructose corn syrup conditionally recommended
claims.quote: Limiting high-fructose corn syrup intake is conditionally recommended for patients with gout, regardless of disease activity.

claims.text: Joint injection and oral steroids are both first-line options (FAQ)
claims.quote: glucocorticoids (oral, intraarticular, or intramuscular) as appropriate first-line therapy for gout flares
